target = 4

target = 3

## conditional receive hold-off's A/B

Upstream, 4 Test Connections of row 4, on the whole host; reported, not judged. udpstp's Server as it ships (H4uab), whose Load Receiver holds off only where more than one datagram is due within its hold-off (conditional receive hold-off), against the same Server with `UDPSTP_ENGINE_HOLD_OFF_US=250` (H4uab250), whose Load Receiver holds off after every turn that read, as before conditional receive hold-off. Their runs went in pairs, one of each, the first of a pair taking turns; udpstp's Clients ran with `UDPSTP_ENGINE_HOLD_OFF_US=250` in both.

The Server's CPU per Load PDU is its process's CPU time and the whole host's softirq and irq time, over the window in which every Test Connection ran, per Load PDU it received there (those planned, as delivered); where the kernel accounts IRQ time, a softirq's time counts once, as softirq time. Its wake-ups are its threads' voluntary context switches over the same window, per Load PDU: the arms ran the two policies only where they are clearly lower with conditional receive hold-off. The Clients' unsent Load PDUs are the median valid run's, and the worst run's of all; lost ones are those the Server host accounts for and those only the path can have lost, the median valid run's. The softirqs and interrupts are per 1,000 Load PDUs received, over the whole run, the median valid run's: NET_RX from /proc/softirqs; LOC (the local timer), RES (rescheduling) and CAL (function-call) interrupts and the NIC's queues' (70 (eth0) on logical CPU 0, as found) from /proc/interrupts.

## conditional receive hold-off's A/B

Upstream, 4 Test Connections of row 4, on the whole host; reported, not judged. udpstp's Server as it ships (H4uab), whose Load Receiver holds off only where more than one datagram is due within its hold-off (conditional receive hold-off), against the same Server with `UDPSTP_ENGINE_HOLD_OFF_US=250` (H4uab250), whose Load Receiver holds off after every turn that read, as before conditional receive hold-off. Their runs went in pairs, one of each, the first of a pair taking turns; udpstp's Clients ran with `UDPSTP_ENGINE_HOLD_OFF_US=250` in both.

The Server's CPU per Load PDU is its process's CPU time and the whole host's softirq and irq time, over the window in which every Test Connection ran, per Load PDU it received there (those planned, as delivered); where the kernel accounts IRQ time, a softirq's time counts once, as softirq time. Its wake-ups are its threads' voluntary context switches over the same window, per Load PDU: the arms ran the two policies only where they are clearly lower with conditional receive hold-off. The Clients' unsent Load PDUs are the median valid run's, and the worst run's of all; lost ones are those the Server host accounts for and those only the path can have lost, the median valid run's. The softirqs and interrupts are per 1,000 Load PDUs received, over the whole run, the median valid run's: NET_RX from /proc/softirqs; LOC (the local timer), RES (rescheduling) and CAL (function-call) interrupts and the NIC's queues' (70 (eth0) on logical CPU 0, as found) from /proc/interrupts.

## conditional receive hold-off's A/B

Upstream, 4 Test Connections of row 4, on the whole host; reported, not judged. udpstp's Server as it ships (H4uab), whose Load Receiver holds off only where more than one datagram is due within its hold-off (conditional receive hold-off), against the same Server with `UDPSTP_ENGINE_HOLD_OFF_US=250` (H4uab250), whose Load Receiver holds off after every turn that read, as before conditional receive hold-off. Their runs went in pairs, one of each, the first of a pair taking turns; udpstp's Clients ran with `UDPSTP_ENGINE_HOLD_OFF_US=250` in both.

The Server's CPU per Load PDU is its process's CPU time and the whole host's softirq and irq time, over the window in which every Test Connection ran, per Load PDU it received there (those planned, as delivered); where the kernel accounts IRQ time, a softirq's time counts once, as softirq time. Its wake-ups are its threads' voluntary context switches over the same window, per Load PDU: the arms ran the two policies only where they are clearly lower with conditional receive hold-off. The Clients' unsent Load PDUs are the median valid run's, and the worst run's of all; lost ones are those the Server host accounts for and those only the path can have lost, the median valid run's. The softirqs and interrupts are per 1,000 Load PDUs received, over the whole run, the median valid run's: NET_RX from /proc/softirqs; LOC (the local timer), RES (rescheduling) and CAL (function-call) interrupts and the NIC's queues' (70 (eth0) on logical CPU 0, as found) from /proc/interrupts.

Its wake-ups are its threads' voluntary context switches over the same window, per Load PDU: the arms ran the two policies only where they are clearly lower with conditional receive hold-off. Its wake-ups are its threads' voluntary context switches over the same window, per Load PDU: the arms ran the two policies only where they are clearly lower with conditional receive hold-off. Their runs went in pairs, one of each, the first of a pair taking turns; udpstp's Clients ran with `UDPSTP_ENGINE_HOLD_OFF_US=250` in both.

The Server's CPU per Load PDU is its process's CPU time and the whole host's softirq and irq time, over the window in which every Test Connection ran, per Load PDU it received there (those planned, as delivered); where the kernel accounts IRQ time, a softirq's time counts once, as softirq time. Its wake-ups are its threads' voluntary context switches over the same window, per Load PDU: the arms ran the two policies only where they are clearly lower with conditional receive hold-off. The Clients' unsent Load PDUs are the median valid run's, and the worst run's of all; lost ones are those the Server host accounts for and those only the path can have lost, the median valid run's. ## conditional receive hold-off's A/B

Upstream, 4 Test Connections of row 4, on the whole host; reported, not judged. udpstp's Server as it ships (H4uab), whose Load Receiver holds off only where more than one datagram is due within its hold-off (conditional receive hold-off), against the same Server with `UDPSTP_ENGINE_HOLD_OFF_US=250` (H4uab250), whose Load Receiver holds off after every turn that read, as before conditional receive hold-off. Their runs went in pairs, one of each, the first of a pair taking turns; udpstp's Clients ran with `UDPSTP_ENGINE_HOLD_OFF_US=250` in both.

The Server's CPU per Load PDU is its process's CPU time and the whole host's softirq and irq time, over the window in which every Test Connection ran, per Load PDU it received there (those planned, as delivered); where the kernel accounts IRQ time, a softirq's time counts once, as softirq time. Its wake-ups are its threads' voluntary context switches over the same window, per Load PDU: the arms ran the two policies only where they are clearly lower with conditional receive hold-off. The Clients' unsent Load PDUs are the median valid run's, and the worst run's of all; lost ones are those the Server host accounts for and those only the path can have lost, the median valid run's. The softirqs and interrupts are per 1,000 Load PDUs received, over the whole run, the median valid run's: NET_RX from /proc/softirqs; LOC (the local timer), RES (rescheduling) and CAL (function-call) interrupts and the NIC's queues' (70 (eth0) on logical CPU 0, as found) from /proc/interrupts.

## conditional receive hold-off's A/B

Upstream, 4 Test Connections of row 4, on the whole host; reported, not judged. udpstp's Server as it ships (H4uab), whose Load Receiver holds off only where more than one datagram is due within its hold-off (conditional receive hold-off), against the same Server with `UDPSTP_ENGINE_HOLD_OFF_US=250` (H4uab250), whose Load Receiver holds off after every turn that read, as before conditional receive hold-off. Their runs went in pairs, one of each, the first of a pair taking turns; udpstp's Clients ran with `UDPSTP_ENGINE_HOLD_OFF_US=250` in both.

The Server's CPU per Load PDU is its process's CPU time and the whole host's softirq and irq time, over the window in which every Test Connection ran, per Load PDU it received there (those planned, as delivered); where the kernel accounts IRQ time, a softirq's time counts once, as softirq time. Its wake-ups are its threads' voluntary context switches over the same window, per Load PDU: the arms ran the two policies only where they are clearly lower with conditional receive hold-off. The Clients' unsent Load PDUs are the median valid run's, and the worst run's of all; lost ones are those the Server host accounts for and those only the path can have lost, the median valid run's. The softirqs and interrupts are per 1,000 Load PDUs received, over the whole run, the median valid run's: NET_RX from /proc/softirqs; LOC (the local timer), RES (rescheduling) and CAL (function-call) interrupts and the NIC's queues' (70 (eth0) on logical CPU 0, as found) from /proc/interrupts.
